[Jia et al. 2026](./#p=jia2026faithfulness) split the requirement on a trace $(P,C,A)$ (prompt, CoT, answer) into *sufficiency*, $H(A\mid C)$ is low; *completeness*, $I(P;A\mid C)\approx 0$, so that $C$ screens off $P$ from $A$ (an unverbalized hint is a completeness failure, which ties this cluster to cluster 2); and *necessity*, perturbing $C$ changes $A$.
[Wang et al. 2026a](./#p=wang2026case), with instruction $Z$, CoT $X$ and answer $Y$: the process is faithful if $p(x,y\mid z)=p(x\mid z)\,p(y\mid x)$, equivalently $Y\perp Z\mid X$.

[Tutek et al. 2025](./#p=tutek2025measuring): $\mathrm{ff}_{\text{hard}}=\mathbb{1}\big[\exists\,r_i:\ y\neq y^{(i)*}\big]$ and $\mathrm{ff}^{(i)}_{\text{soft}}=p(y\mid M)-p(y\mid M^{(i)*})$, where $M^{(i)*}$ is the model after unlearning step $r_i$ and $y^{(i)*}$ its prediction.

[Kudo et al. 2024](./#p=kudo2024llms): $t^{*}(v_i)=\min\{t\mid\max_l\mathrm{acc}(t,l,v_i)>\tau\}$, the first token position at which a probe at some layer decodes the value $v_i$ with accuracy above $\tau=0.9$; positions are counted from the start of the CoT, so a negative $t^*$ means the value "is computed before CoT begins".

claims.reason: These tests do not establish faithfulness as a sufficient condition. Both Wiegreffe and Parcalabescu explicitly limit their measurements to necessary properties or self-consistency.
